rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.p: Find the move that uses the majority to create a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.certo: The pawn advances to a6. If the b7-pawn captures it, no black pawn is left in front of the c5-pawn, and it becomes passed.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.revela: The pawn advances to a6: if the b7-pawn captures it, no black pawn is left in front of the c5-pawn, which becomes passed.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.g2h3.1: The king goes to h3 to capture the h4-pawn, but it gives Black a tempo.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.g2h3.2: The a7-pawn advances to a6 and blocks the majority: no white advance creates a passed pawn, and the black king captures the b4-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.g2h3.3: Back to the position: create the passed pawn before Black blocks the majority.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.c5c6.1: The c5-pawn advances to c6, but it is within reach of the b7-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.c5c6.2: The b7-pawn captures on c6. The two white pawns left on the wing cannot create a passed pawn, and the black king reaches them.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.c5c6.3: Back to the position: look for the advance that takes the b7-pawn away from the front of the c5-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.b4b5.1: The b4-pawn advances to b5, but it is within reach of the black king.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.b4b5.2: The black king captures the b5-pawn. The two white pawns left on the wing cannot create a passed pawn, and Black takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.err.b4b5.3: Back to the position: advance the pawn the black king cannot reach.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.fora: That move does not use the majority. Look for a move of the queenside pawns.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.volta: Try again: use the majority to create a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.e1: Attack: a majority means having, on one wing, more pawns than the opponent. With it, you can create a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.e2: A passed pawn has no enemy pawn in front of it, on its own file or the neighbouring ones: only the pieces can stop it.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.e3: This position comes from a game played on Lichess. White has the queenside majority: three pawns against two.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.l0: Now White threatens to capture the b7-pawn with the a6-pawn and promote on b8.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.l1: The b7-pawn captures the a6-pawn, so that the white pawn does not reach b7.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.l2: The c5-pawn advances to c6. No black pawn is in front of it on the b-, c- and d-files: it is a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.l3: The black king cannot catch the pawn, which promotes on c8. The majority gave a pawn and won a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.maioria.l4: With a majority on one wing, advance the pawns until one of them gets through. Here time mattered: one move less, and the a7-pawn blocked the majority.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.p: Find the move that takes the passed pawn forward.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.certo: The pawn advances to a7 and threatens to promote on a8. The black rook must hurry to watch that square.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.revela: The pawn advances to a7: it threatens to promote on a8, and the black rook must hurry to watch that square.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c4.1: The bishop goes to c4, but leaves the fifth rank and clears the way for the rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c4.2: The rook goes to a5, behind the pawn, and attacks it: the bishop is tied to its defence, and Black takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c4.3: Back to the position: advance the passed pawn while the bishop cuts off the rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c6.1: The bishop goes to c6 to watch a8, but leaves the fifth rank.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c6.2: The rook goes to a5, behind the pawn, and attacks it: the pawn is tied to its defence, and Black is better.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5c6.3: Back to the position: advance the passed pawn while the bishop cuts off the rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5d3.1: The bishop goes to d3, but leaves the fifth rank, and the rook gains the way to the a-file.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5d3.2: The rook goes to a5 and attacks the pawn from behind. It is tied to its defence, and Black takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.err.b5d3.3: Back to the position: the bishop is already in the right place; advance the passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.fora: That move uses neither the passed pawn nor the bishop. Look for a move of one of them.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.volta: Try again: advance the passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.e1: Attack: White again, in another game played on Lichess. The a6-pawn is already passed: no black pawn is in front of it.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.e2: A passed pawn advances better with the support of the pieces. Here the b5-bishop stops the c5-rook from reaching the a-file along the fifth rank.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.l0: The c5-rook cannot go to the a-file along the fifth rank: the b5-bishop closes the way.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.l1: The rook goes to c8 to watch the a8-square along the eighth rank.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.l2: The bishop goes to c6 and also watches a8: if the pawn promotes and the rook captures the queen, the bishop captures the rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.apoio.l3: On its own, the passed pawn would be stopped by the rook. With the bishop watching the square in front, it costs Black the rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.p: Find the move that captures a blocked passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.certo: The rook captures the e5-pawn with check, and along the same rank it also attacks the d5-knight.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.revela: The rook captures the e5-pawn with check: along the same rank, it attacks the g5-king and the d5-knight.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e4g4.1: The rook gives check on g4, but captures nothing.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e4g4.2: The king goes to f6 and attacks the e6-bishop. Both passed pawns are still on the board, and White is better.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e4g4.3: Back to the position: capture the passed pawn that no pawn defends.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e6d5.1: The bishop captures the d5-knight, but leaves the square in front of the e5-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e6d5.2: The d1-rook recaptures on d5. The e5-pawn is free to advance, and White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.err.e6d5.3: Back to the position: keep the blockade and capture the passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.fora: That move does not use the e4-rook. Look for a move of it.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.volta: Try again: capture a blocked passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.e1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side, in another game played on Lichess. White has two passed pawns, on d6 and e5.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.e2: The d7-king blocks the d6-pawn, and the e6-bishop blocks the e5-pawn. Blocked by a piece, a passed pawn cannot advance and may become a target.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.l0: The white king must get out of check, and the d5-knight is still attacked.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.l1: The king gets out of check to f4 and attacks the e5-rook.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.l2: The rook captures the d5-knight, defended by the e6-bishop. Black has won a pawn and a knight.
rot.passedPawn.ideia.alvo.l3: Blocked, a passed pawn cannot advance, and the pieces that defend it are tied to it. Before fearing a passed pawn, see whether it is blocked: the position decides.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra.l.2: The c4-pawn advances to c3. No white pawn is in front of it on the b-, c- and d-files: it is a passed pawn.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra.l.3: The white king goes to f2 to try to catch the pawn via e2 and d1.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra.l.4: The pawn advances to c2 and threatens to promote on c1. The white bishop moves on the light squares and cannot reach c1, a dark square.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra.l.5: The majority created the passed pawn, and only the pieces could stop it: here the king arrived too late, and the bishop did not watch the promotion square.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in another game played on Lichess. On the a-, b- and c-files, Black has three pawns against two.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra2.l.2: The pawn advances to a2 and threatens to promote on a1, with the rook behind it.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra2.l.3: The c2-rook captures the pawn, so as not to let it promote.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra2.l.4: The a6-rook captures the a2-rook along the a-file. Black gave the pawn and won a rook.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra2.l.5: A rook behind the passed pawn supports it at every step, and whoever captures it stands on the rook's line.
rot.passedPawn.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: Black again. The a3-pawn is passed, and the a6-rook stands behind it, on the same file.
rot.passedPawn.demos.ligados.l.2: The pawn advances to b3, next to the a3-pawn. If the rook captures it, the b2-king captures the rook: it defends the pawn.
rot.passedPawn.demos.ligados.l.3: The white king goes to d3 to run to c4 and attack the b3-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.demos.ligados.l.4: The a3-pawn advances to a2 and threatens to promote on a1. The white king arrives too late, and the rook cannot stop both pawns.
rot.passedPawn.demos.ligados.l.5: Two passed pawns side by side support each other, and a rook stops only one of them. Advancing the a3-pawn first drew: the rook captured the b4-pawn with check.
rot.passedPawn.demos.ligados.1: Attack demonstration: Black again, in another game played on Lichess. The a3- and b4-pawns are passed and side by side.
rot.passedPawn.demos.desvio.l.2: The bishop goes to b6 and attacks the e3-bishop. If White does not capture it, the black bishop captures on e3 with check, and the pawn promotes.
rot.passedPawn.demos.desvio.l.3: The e3-bishop captures the b6-bishop and leaves the diagonal that watched c1.
rot.passedPawn.demos.desvio.l.4: The pawn promotes on c1 with check. Black gave a bishop and won a queen.
rot.passedPawn.demos.desvio.l.5: When a piece stops the passed pawn, get it out of the way: with an exchange, a check or a pin, it leaves the square it watches.
rot.passedPawn.demos.desvio.1: Attack demonstration: Black again. The c2-pawn is passed and one step from c1, but the e3-bishop watches that square.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.l.3: The knight goes to f4 with check and attacks the g2-pawn.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.l.4: The king has only the f1-square: the e3-bishop is pinned by the queen and cannot capture the knight.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.l.5: The queen captures the g2-pawn, defended by the f4-knight: it is mate.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.l.6: With the pieces on the king, the passed pawn can wait: the attack decided first. Before pushing the passed pawn, see whether there is something stronger: the position decides.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: Black again. Black has a passed pawn on a7, but the white king is in the centre, on e2.
rot.passedPawn.demos.excecao.2: Advancing the pawn would spend a tempo, and White would use it to defend the king. With the king exposed, look at the checks first.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.passado.enunciado: Your d6- and e7-pawns are passed and side by side. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.passado.fim: The d6-pawn advanced and attacked the e8-rook. The king came to defend it, and the pawn promoted on d8: two passed pawns side by side support each other.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.passado.err.e1d1: 39.Rd1? attacks the d3-pawn, but 39...Rd4 defends the d3-pawn and attacks the d6-pawn: Black takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.passado.err2: 40.dxe8=Q+? captures the rook, but 40...Kxe8 recaptures and attacks the e7-pawn: White loses both passed pawns and the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.alvo.enunciado: White has a passed pawn on d7, blocked by the d8-rook. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.alvo.fim: The rook captured the blocked passed pawn and defended the d8-rook. The white queen fled to a6, and the rook gave check on the first rank, with no flight square for the king.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.alvo.err.f7f8: 26...Rff8? leaves the passed pawn alive: 27.Qc7 supports it, and White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Your d3-pawn is passed and close to promotion, but the white king, on e1, has few squares. Does the passed pawn count here, or the king? Play as Black.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Here the king counted: the bishop gave check on c3, the king had only d1, and the rook gave mate on f1. The passed pawn could wait.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.d3d2: 38...d2+? pushes the passed pawn, but 39.Kxd2 captures it, and the attack is over: White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.f8f2: 38...Rf2? attacks the g2-pawn, but 39.Rxd4 captures the bishop: White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.d4f2: 38...Bf2+? 39.Kd2 gets out of check and attacks the d3-pawn: White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err.f8e8: 38...Re8+? 39.Kd2 gets out of check and attacks the d3-pawn: White takes the advantage.
rot.passedPawn.pratica.valeAqui.err2: 39...d2? pushes the passed pawn, but 40.Kc2 takes the king off the first rank, and White wins the pawn later. 39...Rf1# was mate.
